learning: Two identical-geometry races with this controller gave 399.7 both times, so the package is reproducible. The controller, not the geometry, drove the iteration 10 drop. Bend max_error remains on its plateau, and no geometry lever tested so far has moved it below 0.06 m.
notes: Restores the iteration 9 controller (kd 0.375) on the iteration 7 and 9 geometry. Iteration 10 showed that kd 0.33 drops oval progress to 0.727, so kd is held at 0.375. This is the proven, reproducible package for the final race.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the package I deliver is the one the unseen-track race will score. The best evidence is iteration 7 and iteration 9, which raced the identical geometry and controller and both scored 399.7, with oval progress 0.995 and 20 of 20 oval finishes. Iteration 10 changed only kd (0.375 to 0.33) and fell to 239.3, with oval progress 0.727 and 6 of 20 finishes. So kd 0.33 is the wrong direction, and the 0.375 damping is the stable point on this geometry. I therefore restore the iteration 9 controller exactly: base_speed 1.15, kp 3.75, ki 0.21, kd 0.375, weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, last_direction. The geometry matches the Builder's proposal and the proven iteration 7 and 9 design: 50 mm span at 12.5 mm pitch, 12 mm footprints, y 0.05, wheel_track 0.10, body 0.14 by 0.12 m, mass 0.7 kg, wheel radius 0.03 m. Bend max_error stays on its 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau under every geometry and controller change tested, so no untested lever is worth risking on the final race. The 60 mm span (iterations 3 and 8) and the y 0.03 lead (iteration 1) both collapsed progress and are rejected. Expected result is the iteration 9 outcome: a score near 400, oval progress about 0.995, and the bend tracks still off-track. This is a deliberate reproduction of the best known package, not an exploratory change.
